I couldn't open the three linked sources (the Wikipedia 2026 elections page, the Metaculus FAQ and Metaculus question 46051). What follows comes from news reports. General Election Day is **November 3, 2026**. In-person early voting has already started in some places (D.C. began around October 9), and more states open it over the coming weeks.

**Status quo (as of October 15, 2026): no confirmed event that meets the criteria. On current information this resolves No.**

**Most recent news**
- **October 8–14, D.C. drop-box incident (the closest call so far).** A photo of armed National Guard troops surrounding a D.C. ballot drop box outside the Foggy Bottom Metro station went viral. Why it probably doesn't count:
  - Drop-box-only sites are explicitly excluded by the question.
  - The Guard says the troops were not trying to guard the box, and Snopes found no evidence to suggest the National Guard members seen in the video had been assigned to guard the ballot drop box.
  - The Washington Post's caption, though, said the video showed soldiers in front of an early-voting site. Check whether that spot is also an in-person voting site.
  - Joint Task Force-DC says its service members are directed not to monitor or secure polling locations. The D.C. Board of Elections formally asked the Guard to keep away from drop boxes and other voting locations.
  - This matters going forward: National Guard troops have been patrolling Washington, D.C., since August 2025, so more chance sightings near polling places are likely. The open question for resolution is whether a sighting is "deliberate" or "incidental."
- **October 2, Pentagon ("War Department").** It said it has no plans to send active‑duty troops or federalized National Guard to polling places. Meanwhile, Trump has floated the idea of using federal forces at the polls and invoking the Insurrection Act. Asked on October 1 whether he'd rule out declaring an emergency before the midterms, he said "We'll see".
- **About October 7, mixed signals.** FBI Director Patel declined to rule out deploying FBI agents to voting sites. DHS says ICE won't patrol polling places but could respond to threats or serve warrants nearby. The Justice Department will continue sending federal personnel to polling locations as part of its election-monitoring efforts. DOJ monitors are normally unarmed, but an armed one would be a Yes risk. An NAACP lawsuit over this is at an early stage.
- **Earlier in the year.**
  - February 25: DHS official Heather Honey said "There will be no ICE presence at polling locations for this election."
  - July 30: DHS repeated that "ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations."
  - May: asked by PBS about sending ICE or the Guard to polling sites, Trump said he would "do anything" (the quote is cut off in the source).
  - Steve Bannon has called for ICE to "surround the polls."

**Legal background and base rates**
- Federal law bars sending "troops or armed men at any place where a general or special election is held", with narrow exceptions.
- In modern U.S. elections, deliberate armed federal or state deployments to polling sites essentially don't happen, so the base rate is very low.
- Several blue states have passed extra bans, e.g. New Mexico.
- Watch Republican governors' state police (e.g., Texas DPS) and Guard deployments in Republican-run states, though I found no reporting of plans to station them at voting sites.

**Coming up before resolution**
- More states open early voting through late October.
- Election Day is November 3.
- Possible rulings in the NAACP case.
- Possible emergency or Insurrection Act declarations.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any market prices.

criterios:
This question resolves as **Yes** if active duty United States military personnel, National Guard members, federal officers, or state troopers are deployed by the U.S. federal government or a Republican state governor to any polling or early-voting site, while that site is open for in-person voting for the [2026 general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_elections).

In order to count, the personnel or troops must be armed with firearms and must be either inside the voting site or within 250 feet of its entrance.
letra_pequena:
For purposes of this question, deliberate deployment for any stated reason counts regardless of stated purpose (e.g., ICE officers enforcing immigration laws or National Guard with the stated purpose of protecting voters).

State troopers are defined as law enforcement officers working for state-level law enforcement agencies. Officers of sub-state level agencies such as county sheriff’s departments or municipal police departments do not count.

A deployment by a Republican state governor counts if it is ordered by the governor or, in cases where the deployment order is issued by another state official, when it is specifically authorized by the governor. 

Personnel present in a personal capacity (such as voting or serving as poll workers) do not count.

Personnel whose physical closeness to a polling location is incidental to their other duties, including personnel passing through an area, would not count, as long as their presence is coincidental and unrelated to that site or there is a lack of uncontroversial credible reporting that they were deliberately deployed there.

This question will resolve based upon reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

Locations used solely as drop boxes for mail-in or absentee ballots do not count.

***
This question's information (resolution criteria, fine print, background info, etc) is synced with an [original identical question](https://www.metaculus.com/questions/46051) which opened on 2026-10-12 17:00:00. This question will resolve based on the resolution criteria and fine print of the linked original question. However, if this question would resolve differently than the original question, then this question will be annulled. Additionally, if the original question's resolution could have been known before this question opened, then this question will be annulled.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About three weeks until Election Day on November 3, with some early-voting sites already open. Reporting after Election Day may be needed to establish what happened.

(b) **Status quo:** No confirmed deployment meets the criteria, so the outcome would be **No** if nothing changes.

(c) **Reference class:** Deliberate deployments of armed federal personnel or governor-authorized state troopers to U.S. polling sites in modern elections appear exceptionally rare. I would put the historical base rate for a comparable election at only a few percent, while allowing for elevated risk this year given the administration’s statements.

(d) **No scenario:** Officials follow their stated plans to keep armed personnel away from voting sites. Any further sightings are incidental, at drop boxes only, or cannot be credibly established as deliberate deployments.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Federal officers or troops, or state troopers specifically authorized by a Republican governor, are deliberately sent to protect or conduct an operation at an open in-person voting site while armed.

(f) **Decisive technicalities:** The personnel must have firearms and be inside the site or within 250 feet of its entrance. A drop-box-only location does not count; neither does coincidental proximity. A deployment for a purpose other than election security *does* count if it meets the other criteria.

Probability: 10%

(a) **Time left:** About 19 days until Election Day on November 3, though reporting afterward could establish whether a deployment occurred.

(b) **Status quo:** No qualifying deployment has been confirmed, so the outcome is **No** if nothing changes.

(c) **Reference class:** Deliberate armed federal or governor-authorized state deployments to open U.S. polling sites are exceptionally rare in modern elections. That low base rate matters, even with the heightened concern this year.

(d) **No scenario:** Agencies follow their stated plans to stay away from polling sites. Any further sightings involve incidental patrols or drop-box-only locations.

(e) **Yes scenario:** Federal officials deliberately station armed agents at an open voting site, or a Republican governor authorizes armed state troopers there, and credible reporting confirms it.

(f) **Decisive technicalities:** Personnel must have firearms and be inside the site or within 250 feet of its entrance *while in-person voting is open*. Incidental proximity, a drop-box-only location, or state officers deployed without the governor’s specific authorization would not qualify.

Probability: 9%

**(a) Time left:** Election Day is November 3, 2026, about 19 days away. Early in-person voting is already under way in some places. Credible reporting after the fact may take a few more days or weeks.

**(b) Status quo:** No qualifying event has been confirmed. The D.C. drop-box incident does not count, because drop-box-only sites are excluded and the Guard says the troops' presence was accidental. If nothing changes, this resolves No.

**(c) Reference class:** Deliberate deployments of armed federal troops or officers, or state troopers, to US polling sites in modern general elections. 18 U.S.C. §592 bars stationing "troops or armed men" where an election is held. The base rate is essentially zero in recent decades: well under 2% per cycle. That baseline should be raised for 2026 because of:
- Trump's "I don't rule anything out" rhetoric;
- ongoing Guard deployments in D.C. and Memphis;
- ICE and Border Patrol surge operations in several cities;
- Patel declining to rule out FBI agents at voting sites.

**(d) No scenario:** The Pentagon and DHS stick to their stated policies: no troops at polls and no ICE operations targeting polling places. Guard patrols in D.C. and Memphis are told to stay away from voting locations, as JTF-DC already says it does. DOJ monitors are unarmed. Any sightings of officers near polls are ambiguous, reported as incidental, or involve sheriff's deputies or local police, who don't count. This is the most likely path.

**(e) Yes scenario:** A Republican governor (for example in Texas or Florida) orders state troopers to stand at polling places for "election security." Or ICE or FBI agents are credibly reported to have been deliberately stationed outside polling sites in a Democratic city. Or Trump invokes an emergency or the Insurrection Act just before November 3 and Guard units are posted near voting sites.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- The bar is "deliberate deployment." Incidental presence, or a lack of uncontroversial credible reporting that it was deliberate, means No. That makes Yes harder: officials will likely deny intent, as they did in D.C.
- Personnel must be armed and within 250 feet of the entrance while the site is open for in-person voting.
- Drop-box-only sites are excluded.
- Only state-level agencies count. Sheriffs and city police are out.
- Any stated purpose counts, so an announced "protecting voters" trooper detail from a GOP governor would qualify. Many governors and many sites make this the most plausible Yes route.
- The Washington Post described the D.C. location as an early-voting site. If it is one, that could become contested, but the deliberateness test likely still fails.

Overall: the base rate is very low and officials have firmly denied plans, but the environment is unusually charged and there are many possible actors.

Probability: 11%
